must_preserve: core 'W' shape formed by two interlocking V-like ribbons
central overlapping fold with gradient transition
positive-negative space relationship forming internal triangles
brand-recognizable red dominance with orange accent at fold
can_restyle: gradient intensity or hue shift (e.g., softer reds, muted oranges)
background transparency or subtle texture overlay
shadow depth or glow effect around the W
surface material finish (matte, glossy, metallic) as long as form remains clear
must_not_replace_with: cloud, star, heart, or emoji-style symbols
text-only logos without graphical W structure
color_preservation: Primary identity color is vibrant red; orange gradient at central fold must remain visible but can be desaturated or shifted within warm spectrum. Avoid replacing red with non-brand colors like blue, green, or purple unless explicitly themed and still recognizable as WPS.
structure_summary: The icon is a geometrically precise, symmetrical 'W' constructed from two mirrored ribbon-like V-shapes that interlock at the center with a folded overlap. The negative space forms two inverted triangles inside each arm. The structure relies on clean lines, consistent stroke width, and spatial balance — any distortion breaking this symmetry risks losing brand recognition.
risk_notes: Over-theming may obscure the W structure if gradients become too diffuse or edges too rounded
Replacing red entirely will break instant recognition even if shape is preserved
Adding decorative elements inside negative spaces may confuse the iconic triangle voids
Asymmetry or skewed perspective will undermine the logo’s stability and professionalism
